entries.title: Daniel 3:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Nebuchadnezzar dedicates a golden image in Dura. 8 Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego are accused for not worshipping the image. 13 They being threatened, make a good confession. 19 They are cast into the furnace, 24 from which God delivers them. 28 Nebuchadnezzar seeing the miracle blesses God, and advances them.

A.M. 3424. B.C. 580. made. 2:31,32; 5:23; Ex 20:23; 32:2-4,31; De 7:25; Jud 8:26,27; 1Ki 12:28 2Ki 19:17,18; Ps 115:4-8; 135:15; Isa 2:20; 30:22; 40:19-31; 46:6 Jer 10:9; 16:20; Ho 8:4; Hab 2:19; Ac 17:29; 19:26; Re 9:20 in the province. 30; 2:48; Es 1:1

entries.title: Daniel 3:3
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
the princes.{Achashdarpenaya,} rendered lieutenants in Es 3:12, etc., probably {chief satraps or viceroys} from the Persian {achash} great, eminent, and {sitrab}, a satrap.

Ps 82:1-8; Ac 19:34,35; Ro 1:21-28; 3:11; 1Co 1:24-26; Re 13:13-16 Re 17:13,17 the governors.{Signaya} in persian, {shagnah} deputies or lieutenants.

captains.{Pacawatha}, governors of provinces. See Es 3:13.

the judges.{Adargazraya}, chief judges, or senators, from {adar}, great, and Chal. {gezar}, to judge, decree.

the treasurers.{Gedavraya}, written {gizzavraya,} Ezr 7:21, treasurers, from the Persian {gunjvar}.

the counsellors.{Dethavraya,} counsellors, judges, from {dath} in Persian, {dad}, law, and {var}, possessor or guardian.

the sheriffs.{Tiphtaya} probably the same as the Arabic {Mufti} or head officer of law.

entries.title: Daniel 3:4
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: aloud. Chal. with might. 4:14; Pr 9:13-15; Isa 40:9; 58:1 it is commanded. Chal. they command. Ho 5:11; Mic 6:16 O people. 4:1; 6:25; Es 8:9

entries.title: Daniel 3:5
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
the cornet.{Karna,} the horn.

10,15 flute.{Mashrokeetha,} in Syriac, {mashrookeetha,} the [syrinx (syrigx,)] pipe or flute, as Theodotion renders.

dulcimer. or, singing. Chal. symphony.

entries.content: certain. 2:49; 6:13; 1Sa 18:7-11; Es 3:8; Pr 27:4; Ec 4:4 not regarded thee. Chal. set no regard upon thee. Ac 5:28; 17:7

entries.title: Daniel 3:15
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
ye hear. 10 harp.{Kaithros,} in Arabic, {kitharat,} Greek [kithara,] the guitar.

sackbut.{Sabbecha,} [sambuke,] sambuke, a kind of harp.

psaltery.Pesanter, [psalterion,] a stringed instrument struck with a plectrum; probably similar to what is called a psalterium in Egypt, which Hasselquist describes as a large oblique triangle, with two bottoms two inches from each other, and about twenty catguts of different sizes.

dulcimer.{Soomphanya,} probably the same as the Talmudic [c�wmp�wney�h ,] a pipe.

ye fall. Lu 4:7,8 well. 17; Ex 32:32; Lu 13:9 and who. 28,29; 6:16,20; Ex 5:2; 2Ki 18:35; 2Ch 32:15-17; Isa 36:20; 37:23 Mt 27:43 we are. Mt 10:19; Mr 13:11; Lu 12:11; 21:14,15; Ac 4:8-12,19; 5:29; 6:15 Ac 24:10-13

entries.title: Daniel 3:20

in their.Herodotus says the Babylonish dress was a linen tunic, another of woollen, a white short cloak, and a turban.

coats. or, mantles. hats. or, turbans. 21

walking. Isa 43:2 they have no hurt. Chal. there is no hurt in them. Ps 91:3-9; Mr 16:18; Ac 28:5; 1Pe 3:13 the Son of God.Or, as {bar elahin} may be rendered, "a son of the gods," i.e., a divine person or angel.

entries.title: Daniel 3:27
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
the princes. 2,3; 1Sa 17:46,47; 2Ki 19:19; Ps 83:18; 96:7-9; Isa 26:11 Ac 2:6-12; 26:26 upon. Isa 43:2; Heb 11:34 nor was.This miraculous manifestation of Divine power was witnessed by the court and the nation, and was felt as a just punishment on the transgressors, and a signal display of mercy to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, which should operate on all believers to similar acts of faith and confidence in the Lord.

Mt 10:30; Lu 21:17,18; Ac 27:34
